source.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension
source.authors: Dominik Meier; Luca Joshua Francis; Marco Bernhard Kaiser; T. Ruas; Jan Philip Wahle; B. Gipp

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether models resist or follow altered reasoning in an AI-shopkeeper scenario. It does not test the claim versions’ fine-tuning, response-position KL, opening-token bypasses, weight localization, or training interventions, and its measured behavior is not refusal of harmful user requests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes for Targeted Reasoning Replacement (TRR), which swaps choices in a model’s generated reasoning, and for hint-based evaluations. These measure responses to altered reasoning or hints in shopkeeper decisions, not the harmful-request refusal behavior specified by the claim versions. The reported behavioral, probing, and steering results are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper’s cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It cites Qi et al. (2024), an original source, only for its harm-category taxonomy. Its measure is whether reasoning models pick an unsafe shopkeeper action after their own reasoning trace is edited to argue for it (TRR). There is no fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no weight or rank localization and no deepening training. TRR resembles a reasoning-trace prefill, but it targets a three-way agentic choice, not refusal of a harmful user request, so it is a related construct and is recorded under fits_no_version rather than V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that LRMs show a faithfulness–safety tension under Targeted Reasoning Replacement, with more faithful models following unsafe edited reasoning more often. In QwQ-32B they find distinct, anti-correlated L44 directions. Steering the safety direction raises Safe Reasoning by 9 pp without MMLU cost. Resisting manipulation uses redundant pathways, while complying with it uses a single integrated pathway.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a shopkeeper benchmark, targeted replacement of generated reasoning, activation probing, and inference-time representation steering. It does not use the original sources’ fine-tuning or per-token KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that the hint-based and TRR evaluations differ across models; LLM-based coherent TRR changes the Safe Reasoning and Faithful Reasoning baselines; and steering effects vary with direction, strength, and attention-mask condition.

fits_no_version.finding: When a model's own reasoning trace is edited to argue for the unsafe option, models often follow it. DeepSeek-R1-Llama-70B rejects it only 12.3% of the time; QwQ-32B rejects it 73.9% of the time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injected reasoning in a reasoning model's trace (a prefill-like intervention) frequently overrides safe agentic choices, with large variation across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Models with higher TRR faithfulness (switching to an edited safe option) show lower safety: DeepSeek 97.5% faithful vs 12.3% safe; QwQ-32B 74.7% vs 73.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In HazMart, faithfulness to edited reasoning trades off against resisting edited unsafe reasoning across models.

fits_no_version.finding: Aggregate Safe Reasoning is lowest for Power Seeking (22.36%) and Weight Exfiltration (29.11%), and highest for Hate/Harass/Violence (65.68%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Resistance to unsafe injected reasoning varies by harm category and is weakest in agentic categories.

fits_no_version.finding: At L44 in QwQ-32B, safety and faithfulness probes reach AUROC 0.94 and 0.78, and the two directions have cosine similarity about -0.45.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In QwQ-32B, distinct anti-correlated activation directions predict resisting versus following tampered reasoning.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering at alpha +3 with the safety direction gives +9 pp Safe and -7 pp Faithful; the faithfulness direction gives +8 pp Faithful and -5 pp Safe. Random vectors move metrics by at most 1.1 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation steering shifts QwQ-32B's resistance to tampered reasoning in opposing directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under corrected Table 4 values, hint-based evaluation raises faithfulness for the Qwen models (QwQ 75.28 to 100; Qwen3 81.79 to 98.63). For DeepSeek it lowers faithfulness (97.53 to 70.27) and raises safety (12.33 to 79.73).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured faithfulness and safety depend on whether trace replacement or prompt hints are used.

fits_no_version.finding: In the attention-mask ablation, the safety rescue survives either the direction alone or the mask alone (0.79 and 0.80; 0.87 combined). Masking lowers faithfulness by 13 to 17 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In QwQ-32B, resisting tampered reasoning uses redundant pathways, while following it requires attending to the tampered span.

record.problems: The behavioral benchmark has 77 human-crafted scenarios, which the authors say limits statistical power. Mechanistic analysis and steering are performed only on QwQ-32B. The authors note that literal word substitution can create incoherent reasoning, and that LLM-based replacement introduces uncertainty and changes the behavioral baselines. The paper reports confidence intervals for some results but not all.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The appendix’s neutral-task reasoning-length and MMLU results are not included because they are not measures of the claim’s specified safety behavior. Appendix F’s joint steering-plane maxima are not included as separate rows because the reported main intervention and attention-mask outcomes are recorded above.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on harmful-request compliance.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilled compliant openings, suffixes or decoding changes defeating refusal of harmful user requests. TRR edits reasoning in an agentic choice task instead.
Localization of safety in few weights or ranks. The study examines activation directions only.
Data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
Training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens, and its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper only borrows Qi et al.'s harm taxonomy and never discusses shallow alignment. The main correction is Table 4: the reader misaligned its columns, and the corrected values match the main-text figures (QwQ 73.67% safe, DeepSeek 97.53% faithful and 12.33% safe). TRR is the closest construct to V4 (an injected compliant trace), but the setting is an agentic three-option choice, not harmful-request refusal, and there is no non-tampered refusal baseline in that sense. It is therefore not linked.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples and its effect on harmful-request compliance.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful-request compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses of refusal. TRR manipulates generated reasoning, not these interventions.
Localization of safety behavior in a small set of weights or ranks. The paper studies activation directions, not weight or rank localization.
Whether data or a training objective produces shallow safety.
Training safety beyond the first response tokens and testing whether that training holds up.
